draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Dudhsagar Falls! The name means 'Sea of Milk', and this four-tiered waterfall on the Mahadayi River drops 310 metres, making it one of India's tallest. It sits at the top of a crescent-shaped valley wrapped in forest.
draft.hungryLine: There's nothing to eat out here in my notes, so pack some food, ideally Goa's favourite, rice and fish curry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The falls are just a 5 minute walk from here, and Dudh Sagar Water Falls railway station is only a minute beyond.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a rock, look up at the 30-metre-wide curtain of water and just let the forest noise take over.
moodReplies.surprise-me: There are three tiny railway stations in the Braganza Ghats around here, and one of them exists just to serve the falls.

tips.title: Carry water and snacks.
tips.body: The little stations here lack water and sanitation, so bring what you need.

tips.title: Come by rail or road.
tips.body: The falls are on the Belagavi to Vasco da Gama line, about 46 km east of Madgaon, or 60 km from Panaji by road.

story.title: Sea of Milk
story.body: The Mahadayi River tumbles down four tiers at the head of a crescent-shaped valley. The name Dudhsagar literally means Sea of Milk.

story.title: Stations in the ghats
story.body: The Belagavi to Vasco da Gama line climbs through the Braganza Ghats past the falls. Three small stations, Sonalium, Dudh Sagar and Dudhsagar Waterfalls, serve the area.

story.title: A new taluka announced
story.body: On 25 March 2010 the Chief Minister announced a new Dharbandora taluka, Goa's 12th, in his budget speech.

story.title: Dharbandora is born
story.body: Dharbandora taluka came into being on 4 April 2011, drawing villages such as Colem and Molem from Sanguem taluka.
